In a file that imports from `vitest`, a function returned from `beforeEach` or `beforeAll` runs as teardown, as in Vitest. Before Bun 1.5 it was ignored. `mockClear()`, `vi.spyOn()` and the like return the mock, so an arrow function without braces makes Bun call it.

`--fix` adds the braces, or removes the `return`.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/no-mock-returned-from-hook" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import { beforeEach, vi } from "vitest";

beforeEach(() => send.mockClear());
beforeEach(() => vi.spyOn(process, "exit"));
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { beforeEach, vi } from "vitest";

beforeEach(() => {
  send.mockClear();
});
beforeEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks());
beforeEach(() => {
  const server = listen();
  return () => server.close();
});
```
